subject: NovaEdge MAP & eval cadence — staircase ramp pricing and discount ask
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <aramos@novaedge.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Lopez <mlopez@novaedge.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novaedge.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP request & eval cadence for Redwood POC

Sean —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, NovaEdge is preparing an evaluation plan to validate latency and cost at our 50k qps-infer profile. High level: 4-week technical evaluation (hosted), followed by a 3-month pilot (dedicated pool) and then a 12–24 month staged commit depending on perf and unit economics.

Procurement needs a simple staircase pricing schedule aligned to MAP milestones and a clear statement of what discount thresholds require exec sign-off. To be explicit: discounts >15% need CFO authorization, >25% require CEO approval at NovaEdge. Please include milestone KPIs tied to ramp (e.g., 25% commit at 3mo, 50% at 9mo, full at 18mo).

Attached: procurement_terms.pdf with their standard SOW checklist.

Can you send a formal pricing table we can put on our internal approval docket by Friday? We need the MAP document (final) and a short summary for legal/procurement.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Cloud Partnerships
NovaEdge Systems

Attachments: procurement_terms.pdf (pdf, 128KB)
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <aramos@novaedge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP request & eval cadence for Redwood POC

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. Draft attached: NovaEdge_MAP_v3.pdf and License_Tiers.xlsx — these show a proposed staircase: 10% discount on initial pilot commitment, an incremental 8% at the 50% ramp milestone, and a further 4% at final commit for an effective year-one discount of up to 20% under the standard terms.

Given the strategic nature and the expected $1.8M ARR first-year commit, procurement is asking if we can compress incentives (higher up-front discount) to secure an earlier commit. To be transparent, the internal floor for negotiated discounts without exec approval is 15%. I'm looping Marissa and Karthik for approval beyond that — specifically we will likely need CFO approval for anything above 18% and CEO for >22%.

Ask: can Marissa/Karthik weigh in on approving a one-time concession to 22% effective year-one discount if NovaEdge signs a minimum 18-month committed ramp and prepays 50%? I can push that as an executive concession tied to specific KPIs in the MAP.

I attached the MAP with milestone KPIs and the license tier sheet for procurement.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: NovaEdge_MAP_v3.pdf, License_Tiers.xlsx
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: NovaEdge MAP & eval cadence — discount approval needed

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Alicia's ask and the draft MAP. TL;DR: 18-month ramp commitment ask; initial year ARR ~ $1.8M; procurement pushing for deeper concession (targeting ~22% effective). NovaEdge has clear internal thresholds: >15% CFO sign-off, >25% CEO sign-off — they're stricter than usual.

Why 22%? They want a larger up-front concession so their board can approve a faster procurement window. If we offer 22% effective Y1 discount, they move pilot start earlier and accelerate the pilot acceptance criteria to 4 weeks (technical) + commit in 3 months.

Risk/benefit: at 22% our unit economics are tight for the first two quarters but the multiyear LTV looks solid if they scale. Proposed structure: 20% max out-the-gate if they prepay 6 months; additional 2% rebate when they hit the 50% ramp KPI at month 9.

Can you advise/approve: up-front concession up to 20% (no exec needed) vs. conditional up to 22% (needs exec escalation). If you approve 22% conditional, I'll prototype the language in the MAP tying the extra 2% to the 50% ramp milestone and prepayment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync if helpful.

— Sean
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: NovaEdge MAP & eval cadence — discount approval needed

Sean —

Thanks for the context. I support giving them room to sign quickly. Approve up to 18% upfront (no further sign-off). For anything above 18% and up to 20%, we can treat as a finance-authorized concession (Karthik to approve). For 21%–22% we need an executive exception tied to concrete guardrails: 18-month committed term, 50% prepayment for the first 6 months, and a milestone escrow clause if they miss the KPIs.

If you can get them to accept those guardrails, I will back an executive exception pitch to the CRO and CEO for the extra 1–2%. Please make the MAP language explicit about the milestone triggers and the payment cadence. Also call out that the extra rebate is earned (rebate/credit) only after verified usage at the checkpoint — no retroactive discount to prior invoices.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (212) 555-0198

(Feel free to loop Legal for milestone wording; I want a short, clear clause we can include in the SOW.)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: NovaEdge MAP & eval cadence — discount approval needed

Team —

Reviewed the numbers. I will authorize a finance-level concession up to 20% effective year-one discount provided the following are in place:
- 12-month minimum committed term (we prefer 18 months but will accept 12 for partial approval)
- 50% prepayment for first 6 months or a letter of credit
- Clear KPI verification process for the 50% ramp milestone (logs and latency SLAs)

If Sean secures acceptance of the above and NovaEdge still requires >20% (to reach 22%), escalate to CEO for final sign-off. On the CEO ask, we will need a concise one-page business case: ARR impact, payback schedule, and why this concession accelerates an outcome materially above our baseline.

I approve up to 20% now. Please confirm in writing when NovaEdge accepts the guardrails and share the updated MAP + procurement docs.

Karthik Iyer
CFO | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: NovaEdge financials (internal) [not included in thread].
